title: Runner host action
description: One action a person approves for one enrolled runner to carry out on its host: the action's dotted id from the catalog, the runner that runs it, its parameters (typed per action) and what it does in one plain sentence. It travels inside a signed approval for a pinned run: the approval names this schema, carries the action as its canonical JSON (keys sorted, no whitespace), pins the SHA-256 of that JSON, and the action's runner_id is the run's own. Integers and strings only, so the canonical JSON is the same in every language. The object and every params object are closed: an action can do only what its params say. Catalog: k8s.delete-failed-pods (params.namespace; absent means every namespace); k8s.rollout-restart (params.namespace and params.deployment: restart one deployment and wait for its rollout; the cluster's own namespaces are refused); systemd.user-restart (params.unit: reload the user's systemd manager and restart one user service; Linux only); docker.prune-images (params.until_hours: remove the images unused and older than that many hours; never volumes); gh.cancel-run (params.repo and params.run_id: cancel one GitHub Actions run of an inorbithr repository); iohr.upgrade (no params: the runner upgrades its own iohr the way it was installed); preview.take (params.branch: take one preview-int/, feat/ or fix/ branch into the owner's Preview checkout, then check the Preview app); roll.task (params.rev, params.task and params.services: run one roll task at one commit of main on the deploy server); build.sweep-targets (params.mode: cap or guard the Rust build output of the core checkout and its worktrees); gh.release-rerun (params.run_id: re-run the failed jobs of one failed sdk release run whose commit passed its examples). Draft line: it may still be corrected.

action.description: The action's id from the catalog: lower-case dotted words, for example k8s.delete-failed-pods.

runner_id.description: The enrolled runner that runs it: rnr_ and a ULID, the same as the run's runner_id.

params.description: The action's parameters; their shape is the action's (see the catalog below).

effect.description: What it does, one plain sentence a person reads before approving, for example: Deletes every failed pod in namespace example.

k8s-delete-failed-pods.description: k8s.delete-failed-pods: delete the pods in phase Failed. namespace names one namespace; absent, every namespace.

namespace.description: A Kubernetes namespace name: lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, at most 63.

k8s-rollout-restart.description: k8s.rollout-restart: restart deployment `deployment` in namespace `namespace` and wait for it to roll out. The cluster's own namespaces (kube-system, kube-public, kube-node-lease) are refused by the runner. Effect, as a person reads it: Restarts deployment example in namespace example and waits for the new pods.

namespace.description: A Kubernetes namespace name: lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, at most 63.

deployment.description: A deployment's name in that namespace: lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, at most 63.

systemd-user-restart.description: systemd.user-restart: reload the user's systemd manager, then restart one user service. Linux only; a runner on any other system refuses it. Effect, as a person reads it: Restarts the user service example.service on the runner's host.

unit.description: A user service unit: lower-case letters, digits and @ . _ -, ending in .service, at most 71 characters.

docker-prune-images.description: docker.prune-images: remove every image no container uses that is older than until_hours. Never volumes, networks or a system prune. Effect, as a person reads it: Removes the unused Docker images older than 24 hours on the runner's host.

until_hours.description: Only images created more than this many hours ago: 1 to 720 (30 days).

gh-cancel-run.description: gh.cancel-run: cancel one GitHub Actions workflow run, with the runner host's own GitHub sign-in. Effect, as a person reads it: Cancels GitHub Actions run 1 of inorbithr/example.

repo.description: The repository, owner/name, of the inorbithr organisation only; the name is never . or ..

run_id.description: The workflow run's id: 1 to 2^53 - 1, so it is exact in every language.

iohr-upgrade.description: iohr.upgrade: the runner upgrades its own iohr to the newest release the way it was installed (Homebrew, or the install script's checked archive); never a downloaded script. No params. Effect, as a person reads it: Upgrades iohr on the runner's host to the newest release.

preview-take.description: preview.take: take one branch into the owner's Preview checkout on the runner's host (mise run preview:take: fast-forward, else a merge; it stops on a conflict and changes nothing), then check the Preview app without restarting it (mise run preview:up --check). Effect, as a person reads it: Takes branch feat/example into the Preview checkout and checks the Preview app.

branch.description: The branch on origin: preview-int/, feat/ or fix/ and then lower-case letters, digits and . _ / -, at most 100 after the prefix; never with .. anywhere.

roll-task.description: roll.task: run one roll task at one commit on the deploy server, through the runner host's roll script (it checks the commit is on origin/main, then runs mise run <task> <services> in a checkout of that commit on the server). services is the task's arguments, space-separated; empty means none. Effect, as a person reads it: Runs roll task roll:services at commit 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000 on the deploy server.

task.description: The roll task, one of the catalog's.

services.description: The task's arguments: empty, or up to 32 service names (lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, at most 40 each, never starting with a hyphen, so none is read as an option) separated by one space.

build-sweep-targets.description: build.sweep-targets: bound the Rust build output of the core checkout and its worktrees on the runner's host (build output only; a target in use is never touched). mode cap caps every target now (mise run target:sweep); mode guard sweeps only the targets on a volume that is full enough (mise run target:guard). Effect, as a person reads it: Caps every Rust build target on the runner's host.

gh-release-rerun.description: gh.release-rerun: re-run the failed jobs of one release workflow run of the sdk repository, with the runner host's own GitHub sign-in. The repository is fixed by the runner, never a param. The runner refuses unless the run is the release workflow on main, it concluded failure, and its commit has a green examples-run status. Effect, as a person reads it: Re-runs the failed jobs of sdk release run 100000.

run_id.description: The workflow run's id: 100000 to 2^53 - 1 (six digits or more), so it is exact in every language.
